3.0.0.en: The Apostle cannot speak to them as people who have matured spiritually, but as beginners in the knowledge of Christ, like children with regard to the knowledge of God's wisdom and will, because they are still occupied with fleshly, that is, material, things.

3.1.0.en: Just as milk is given to children because they have no ability to digest the food of adults, so the Apostle Paul spoke to them, as spiritual beginners, only of the basics of Christianity, because they had not yet acquired the ability to enter into the depth of spiritual knowledge.

3.2.0.en: Envy is caused by distorted passions, strife is caused by arguments born of pride and self, and division is the practical behavior that follows from these. The proof that the description of the carnal man applies to them is the presence of envy, strife and factions among them, which are the marks of those who walk according to the desires of the flesh, so that their conduct is equal to the conduct of those who have not yet accepted the faith.

3.2.1.en: Let us look within ourselves to see how far our sensual desires affect our lives. Do we envy others for the material things they own and we do not? Do we quarrel with one another? If so, let us understand that we are still short of the spirituality that the children of the Kingdom must have, that spirituality which is the true goal that every Christian seeks, and which is achieved only when our desires are united with the will of God.

3.3.0.en: In a question of astonishment, he affirms the carnal level by which they live, when some of them form factions by following Paul and others Apollos; their inner motives are still not for Christ.

3.4.s.en: (2) The work of God and the work of the servant

3.4.0.en: By his question, "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos?", the Apostle Paul draws the attention of the people of Corinth to the fact that Paul and Apollos are no more than servants of the Lord, whom He used as a means to deliver His message to them, by the gifts and abilities that the Lord gave to each of them to help them deliver the message.

3.5.0.en: Here the Apostle likens them to a field in which Paul cast the seed of spiritual knowledge that leads to salvation, through his preaching, and then Apollos watered this seed through his spiritual teachings; but the more important work is the work of the Lord, who makes this seed grow, and without His work the harvest cannot be gathered.

3.6.0.en: But Paul and Apollos do not possess the power of making grow, which God alone possesses, and without it the casting of the seed and the watering of it have no result. This does not cancel the work of the servants, but makes clear that success is by the work of God.

3.7.0.en: He who casts the seed or waters it performs a part of one work; therefore this should not be a reason for separate allegiance, that is, division, for the work is one, and each of them will receive a reward from the Lord according to his diligence in the work.

3.8.0.en: Here he again likens them to a field and to a building. Paul and Apollos are each workers whom the Lord uses in tilling the field or in laying the foundation of the building, a work which the Lord accomplishes by His power and will.

3.8.1.en: If you offer service or care to someone, whether in your house for your relatives or in the Church, know that you are an instrument in the hand of God, and that He is the true Father and Shepherd. Therefore ask for His help; do not be proud or boast of what you do, or blame others for not appreciating your labor; thank God for every success that is achieved; and beware of rejoicing in praise and gathering people around you, for you are merely a servant of God, so do not steal His glory and turn it to yourself.

3.9.s.en: (3) Spiritual edification and the evaluation of service

3.9.0.en: "According to the grace of God which is given unto me" as an apostle, I became like a wise masterbuilder, and laid the strong foundation, which is faith in Christ; but everyone who builds good works and services upon this foundation must take heed how he builds, so that his works are done from a pure heart and with faithfulness.

3.10.0.en: No one can lay another foundation in place of the one I laid as the foundation of your spiritual edification, which is faith in Jesus Christ and His Church.

3.11.0.en: Gold, silver, precious stones: heavenly spiritual services that influence those served, because gold signifies heaven, silver the word of God, and precious stones the spiritual virtues. Wood, hay, stubble: social and athletic services and activities that have no purpose or relation to spiritual things; for wood, stubble and hay are materials easily burned and destroyed, signifying all superficial services whose effect quickly comes to an end.

3.12.0.en: The fruits of the service will be evident. The servant of the first kind will have good fruit in those he serves, while the servant of the second kind will not have fruit among those he serves like the first, because his teachings were weak. This will be revealed on the day of judgment (the testing by fire, that is, the divine judgment).

3.13.0.en: If the effect of the service endures in those served and they advance spiritually, the servant will receive a reward in heaven.

3.14.0.en: If those served do not stand firm before the fires of trials and afflictions, that is, if all the labors of the servant are burned up and vanish, and those served are far from God, the servant will lose the reward of his service because it was a superficial and weak service, but he will be saved for the sake of his faith despite his failure in the service. The phrase "he shall be saved" refers to the servant whose service did not bring the desired result, but whose personal life was one of faith and good work, and the phrase "he shall suffer loss" refers to the reward for the service. This shows the importance of the servant's striving in the service, and also shows that there is recompense for works.

3.14.1.en: All the talk is about the labors of the service and their evaluation on the day of judgment: either they are of value and we receive a reward, or they are weak and are burned up, that is, become worthless. It has no relation to the servant's personal salvation, for he will be saved for the sake of his faith, but "so as by fire", that is, barely, because of the absence of good works and of a service of value before God. This does not mean that there is a fire in heaven by which the righteous are tormented before they enter Paradise, as the adherents of the heresy of purgatory claim.

3.15.s.en: (4) The Church is the temple of God

3.15.0.en: Do you not know that you have been sanctified by your membership in the body of Christ, and have become like the Holy of Holies which belongs to the Lord, and His Holy Spirit has descended upon you and dwelt in you by the Holy Myron?

3.16.0.en: If any servant spreads among you the spirit of division and factionalism, he thereby tears the one body, that is, the body of Christ, which is the Church, and this servant will be deprived of the work of the Holy Spirit in him, and his salvation will become difficult.

3.16.1.en: This shows that we as believers do not belong to ourselves but to God. Likewise, whoever insists on defiling his senses and corrupting them by sin wrongs his body, which belongs to God; and our God is just, so He will punish him with destruction and eternal corruption, in addition to the fact that a person is often exposed to diseases that strike his body as a result of falling into sins that harm his body, such as fornication and anger.

3.16.2.en: Keep your senses pure and flee from evil so that you may enjoy a pure body, for it is the temple of God; and if you corrupt it by any sin, hasten to repentance to restore its purity.

3.17.0.en: Let no man deceive himself into thinking that he is wise because of his distinction in intelligence and understanding; by this pride he harms himself and may cause problems and divisions in the Church. He must humble himself before God as a fool, that he may learn spiritual wisdom from Him.

3.18.0.en: The wisdom of this world, which cannot understand the truth of this salvation and redemption accomplished on the Cross, is foolishness itself with God. For it is written that their refusal to accept the true wisdom will in the end lead to the destruction of their souls, so that everyone will see that their earthly wisdom did not achieve salvation for them.

3.19.0.en: Also God knows that earthly wisdom does not help anyone to be saved; it is vain, that is, worthless, for understanding this salvation.

3.19.1.en: To acquire wisdom we must hold fast to our spiritual worship and all works of mercy, and walk in goodness, so that we become fit for wisdom to dwell in us; and when we acquire wisdom we increase in goodness and righteousness, and God grants us still more wisdom. Thus wisdom and goodness each cause the other to grow.

3.20.s.en: (6) All things are yours and you are Christ's

3.20.0.en: Here the Apostle Paul returns and forbids them to follow particular persons, who become the object of their pride and of their admiration for their intellectual or oratorical abilities, because these abilities are gifts from God given to these persons for the benefit of the Church and the salvation of the souls of its members.

3.21.0.en: All the servants, and what is in the world, and life and death, and things present and things to come, are the work of God in the servants and through them for the accomplishment of their salvation. For life, to believers, is an opportunity for communion with God and preparation for eternity, and death is a passage toward the Kingdom.

3.22.0.en: But you are Christ's, who bought you with His precious blood, and He is the Son of the Father by nature and one with Him in essence, and He made us children of God by adoption.

3.22.1.en: Your abilities are divine gifts to you which should be used for the glory of God. So do not neglect them, for they belong to God and He will call you to account for them: did you use them only for your own benefit, or for the benefit of those around you? And what can you offer to the Church while you are heedless of it?

3.22.2.en: Remember, O Lord, Your maidservant: the humility of the servant with those served, and his firmness with them

4.0.0.en: "Let a man so account of us", me and Apollos and the rest of the priests, as servants of Christ, not as masters over you, serving His Church, and entrusted by Him with the Holy Mysteries.

4.0.1.en: The word "mysteries" here means the truths and beliefs that are above the human mind, which man grasps only by faith, such as the seven sacraments of the Church. These truths and beliefs are necessary for the sanctification of man and his preparation for the life of fellowship with God.

4.1.0.en: The most important quality of a steward is to be faithful in the responsibility his master entrusts to him. If this is required in worldly affairs, it is required all the more in spiritual affairs, that is, of spiritual stewards.

4.2.0.en: If the believers of Corinth formed factions for Apollos and Cephas, preferring them to Paul, Paul does not care about their opinions concerning his faithfulness in the service, nor about any human court. He called the human court "man's day", as the divine court is called the day of judgment or the day of the Lord. For the judgments of men are not free of errors in judging matters, and they did not send him or command him to teach; he is not their steward but God's steward. Paul added that he also does not rely on any wisdom in himself, because he knows that he too is imperfect and liable to error and self-indulgence, and that the conscience of any man is not infallible, and therefore he does not judge himself.

4.3.0.en: Although my conscience does not reproach me for any shortcoming in carrying out my apostolic duties in the service, this feeling of mine is not proof of the perfection of my faithfulness in the service and my innocence of shortcoming in the stewardship; I accept only the judgment of the Lord Jesus upon me, for He searches the hearts and knows the intentions, and nothing is hidden from Him.

4.4.0.en: "Therefore judge nothing before the time", whether concerning me or concerning Apollos, and leave this to the day of judgment, and do not give yourselves a right that belongs to God alone, who, when He comes for judgment, will "bring to light the hidden things of darkness", that is, things hidden from sight, and will make manifest the secrets of hearts, and reveal all the works of men and all the thoughts of their hearts; and every man who was faithful inwardly as outwardly will receive from God the praise he deserves.

4.4.1.en: Would that we might benefit from this advice, so that we do not pass judgments on others but leave the judgment to the just Judge, who sees what we cannot see and examines what we cannot examine, so that His judgments are just. As for our own opinions of others, they depend on the appearances of things and do not reach the whole truth, and so they are liable to error.

4.5.0.en: What I said about myself, Paul, and Apollos, as an example for servants in submission and in surrendering our lives to God, I intended so that you may learn to give glory to God, and that none of you be puffed up against another or form a faction and boast, so that divisions arise which harm the Church.

4.6.0.en: Every knowledge or gift in a person is a divine gift and a distinction received as a grant from God, and he has no merit in it. How, then, can there be room for one person to boast over another, as though he had obtained this gift by himself and had not received it as a free gift from God?

4.6.1.en: Thank God for every gift or ability that you enjoy, and be faithful in using it for His glory, so that you help those around you whenever God gives you the opportunity. Learn from the fathers and spiritual servants, but do not become attached to any one of them, for they are the means through which God conveys His blessings to you. Let your heart be attached to God; do not form a faction for any teacher and keep away from, or reject, another, but learn from all, and see God in all their teachings.

4.7.s.en: (3) The pride of the Corinthians and the endurance of the Apostles

4.7.0.en: You have been content with the blessings and spiritual knowledge you have obtained and no longer need more; you thought that you had reached the highest degrees of spiritual grace and had become perfect of yourselves, without help from us the Apostles; and beyond your fullness and self-sufficiency you thought that you had come to reign with Christ, and enjoyed the joys of the Kingdom, and reached the highest degrees of spiritual grace until you thought that you had become kings in the Kingdom of Heaven, and that you had obtained perfect holiness and gained every spiritual blessing. I wish that your illusion were truth, so that we might share with you in the glory and the blessings.

4.8.0.en: "A spectacle unto the world": it mocks us for the insults we endure.

4.8.1.en: "To angels and to men": the angels rejoice in us and the believers among men imitate us.

4.8.2.en: God allowed us the Apostles to be put last of all, as though sentenced to death (the Romans used to put their captives at the end of the triumphal procession); and in truth we have faced death every day for the sake of Christ, and have become a wonder to the beholders because of the severity of our afflictions, and have become an object of mockery to the world, but the object of the admiration of the angels.

4.9.0.en: In this verse and those that follow, the Apostle describes the poor condition of the Apostles and contrasts it with the condition of those Corinthians who imagined that they had become happy. There is clear sarcasm in this, as though he said to them: how great is the difference between us and you; you are at the highest degrees of happiness and we are at the lowest ranks of misery. He says: you consider us unworthy to teach you, and you have become wise, needing no teaching, as if you had gained wisdom by your union with Christ; but we, because of our zeal in serving Christ, are considered by you to be fools. Some accuse us of weakness, but you, in your own opinion, are strong and need the support of no one, and you reckon that you deserve honor and that we deserve contempt.

4.10.0.en: Even to this present hour we the Apostles endure hunger and thirst and other hardships and afflictions, and we have no dwelling place, for we are always sojourners and strangers in our journeys from place to place to preach the Gospel and to flee from the persecutors.

4.11.0.en: We support ourselves by the labor of our hands; Paul used to work at making tents, although he had the right that the Church should support him, as stated in (ch. 9:14), but he did not ask for this; and we repay evil with good and cursing with blessing, and we endure persecution without complaint or murmuring.

4.12.0.en: They ascribe bad qualities to us and we answer with gentle words, imitating Christ, who, when He was reviled, reviled not again; when He suffered, He threatened not, but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously (1 Pet 2:23). We have come to the extreme of contempt and lowliness in the cause of serving Christ and the Church.

4.12.1.en: Do not think that you have arrived at the righteousness and the life that please God, lest you grow lazy in continuing your spiritual striving and growth in the love of God; and look to the fathers and spiritual teachers to learn from them and imitate them.

4.13.0.en: I do not mean by this manner of my writing to shame you, by comparing your condition with our labors the Apostles, and by answering what you imagine of yourselves; rather I speak to you as a father who loves you, and so I warn you that you may return to what is right.

4.14.0.en: Though there are many who take you by the hand to guide you in the spiritual life, you have no spiritual fathers other than me (for Paul was the means of their faith in Christ, by his proclaiming to them the Gospel, the power of God unto salvation). The father is the one who sows the seeds of faith, while the guide follows the believer and takes him by the hand. So I ask you, because I am your spiritual father and you are confident of my love for you and my desire to benefit you, to walk in my way and follow my course in offering my life to the service of Christ.

4.14.1.en: Would that we might be disciples of our spiritual fathers whom we love and trust, so that they may be an example to us in the way of life, and we may imitate them in our conduct and our spirituality.

4.15.s.en: (5) A call to return to what is right

4.15.0.en: "For this cause", that is, that you may remember my way and my teaching, I have sent unto you Timothy, my companion in my journeys and my helper, who is worthy to act on my behalf and is faithful in the service of Christ and His Gospel, to remind you of my ways in Christ, that is, humility and faithfulness to God, and to bring to your attention my teaching, which is one in every place where I have preached.

4.16.0.en: Some proud false teachers claimed that Paul was weak and did not dare to come to Corinth, but he paid no attention to their words and sent his disciple Timothy to confirm his teachings.

4.16.1.en: Do not be shaken by the words of the wicked who oppose the word of God and who describe you as weak and ignorant because of your clinging to God. Stand firm in the teachings of the Church and ask for God's help and wisdom.

4.17.0.en: I will come to you shortly, if the Lord will, and I will reveal to you the disagreement between the works of these men and their words. For Christ gave the Apostles power which appeared repeatedly in miracles, in speaking with tongues, and in their ability to draw people to Christ, whereas the proud false teachers have no such power, and this is proof that God did not send them to that service.

4.18.0.en: For true religion is not mere pretension and confession with the tongue, but a change of heart, a reform of conduct, and a life we live with God.

4.19.0.en: The Apostle Paul left it to them to choose between his coming to them as one who rebukes and reproves, or as a tender comforter. That is, do they want him to come and cut some of them off from the Church as a discipline for them for their opposition and pride, or to come to them with words of forgiveness and peace if they turn away from disputes and quarrels? The authority of the Church and the problem of the fornicator
